tex_content.label: eq:annular-boundary-factor
tex_content.html:
\begin{equation} X_x-iX_y=z^m Q(z),\qquad Q(0)\ne 0 . \end{equation} Here $Q$ is continuous, locally half-Holder, and has weak derivative in $L^2$; it is $C^1$ in the interior.
Proof

The complex differential satisfies $\bar\partial \Phi =A\Phi $. A small-disk Cauchy-transform contraction gives an invertible gauge in which it is holomorphic. At the boundary, a metric row frame and reflection by its anti-complex involution reduce to the same construction. Holomorphic factorization gives (15) and the stated estimates.

Local vanishing would propagate to a constant disk, contradicting the Jordan trace. Zeros are therefore isolated relative to the closed disk; compactness makes them finite. A noninjective monotone label would collapse an arc, on which the tangential differential, and by conformality the full differential, would vanish. Thus the label is injective and hence a homeomorphism.

□

Proof of Theorem 5.3

\proves thm:annular-plateau The preceding lemmas give the same conformal harmonic minimum with a homeomorphic boundary label and within-$C^1$ regularity. Compactness makes it Lipschitz. Hence it is an actual admissible disk, and

\[ A_g(\gamma )\leq \operatorname {Area}_g(u)=E(u)\leq A_g(\gamma ). \]

□
